subject: Learning Methods
title: The Speed Reading Myth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Speed Reading Myth.

hook.text: Speed reading courses promise 1,000 words per minute. Research shows comprehension drops dramatically above 600.

buildup.text: Eye-tracking studies show speed readers skip words. What they call 'reading' is closer to aggressive skimming.

discovery.text: There's a hard bottleneck: language processing speed. Your brain can only decode meaning so fast despite eye speed.

twist.text: The real skill is not reading everything fast. It is knowing when to skim and when to slow down and engage deeply.

climax.text: Flexible reading speed based on purpose and difficulty is far more effective than one constant fast pace.

punchline.text: Speed reading is just skimming with a brand name.

quiz.question: What is the main bottleneck that limits reading speed?
options: Language processing speed in the brain
The font size and page layout
